Solution overview

I tested the Flask fitness application, its eight progression snapshots, and the desktop demo. I also ran the Docker checks through GitHub Actions and Jenkins. Jenkins builds the images but does not deploy or leave the application running.

1. Applicationapp.py, shared app implementation, eight Versions/ snapshots, and the desktop GUI demo.
2. ValidatePytest suite (33 tests), Python compilation, HTTP route checks, and GUI startup check.
3. PackageMulti-stage Dockerfile: isolated test image and non-root Gunicorn runtime image.
4. AutomateGitHub Actions on pushes/PRs and Jenkins Build #9 on the assignment VM; both validate Docker images and tests.

Docker execution on the Linux assignment VM

Run these commands in a terminal inside the Linux assignment VM, from the cloned project directory. Starting Docker activates the daemon; it does not automatically give every service account permission to use Docker.

sudo systemctl start docker
systemctl is-active docker
id -nG

# Build and test the test image
docker build --target test -t aceest-fitness:test .
docker run --rm aceest-fitness:test

# Build, launch, smoke-test on host port 5000, then clean up
docker build --target runtime -t aceest-fitness:latest .
docker run -d --name aceest-fitness-runtime -p 5000:5000 aceest-fitness:latest
curl -i http://127.0.0.1:5000/health
curl -i "http://127.0.0.1:5000/api/plan?weight=70&height=175&age=30&gender=male&activity=moderate&goal=fat_loss"
docker stop aceest-fitness-runtime
docker rm aceest-fitness-runtime

In the VM, the interactive account had Docker group access. The test image reported 33 passing tests; both runtime endpoints returned HTTP 200 on host port 5000, and the temporary container was stopped and removed. This port-5000 execution was rerun and verified on 11 October 2026; the screenshots below show the earlier successful Docker build/test/runtime validation (which used port 5050).

How to execute

1. Set up Python (PowerShell)

python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt

The current GUI demo uses the project runtime dependencies; no additional GUI packages are needed.

Tkinter is included with the standard Windows Python installer when Tcl/Tk support is selected.

2. Run the main Flask app

python app.py

Browse to http://127.0.0.1:5000/health or run curl.exe http://127.0.0.1:5000/health. Stop with Ctrl+C.

3. Run a progressive Flask snapshot

python .\Versions\app_v1_0.py
# Stop it with Ctrl+C before starting another snapshot
python .\Versions\app_v5_0.py

Snapshots run as standalone scripts on port 5000; run one at a time. Available versions: app_v1_0.py, app_v1_1.py, app_v2_0.py, app_v2_1.py, app_v3_0.py, app_v3_1.py, app_v4_0.py, and app_v5_0.py.

4. Run the desktop GUI demo

python .\fitness_gui_demo.py

It opens the desktop client and runs a local Flask API on a temporary port; no separate Flask process is needed. Close the window to stop the API.

5. Repeat validation

python -m pytest -q
python -m compileall -q app.py tests Versions fitness_gui_demo.py

Git process: review, commit, push, verify

The working branch was main, tracking origin/main. The initial GitHub revision was 240e661; the application additions and execution report were local changes. The GitHub repository is malli19960/aceest-fitness-devops.

  1. Review branch and local file changes with git status, git diff --check, and git diff.
  2. Stage only the application, tests, version snapshots, CI/container configuration, and documentation. Keep secrets, local SQLite databases, caches, and reference-only Olderfiles/ out of the push.
  3. Inspect staged paths and patch with git diff --cached --stat and git diff --cached; verify whitespace with git diff --cached --check.
  4. Commit the reviewed changes to main, then publish with git push origin main.
  5. Verify the pushed commit appears on GitHub and check the push-triggered Actions run.
git status
# Stage the explicitly reviewed project files (exclude Olderfiles/)
git add app.py tests Versions Dockerfile .dockerignore .gitignore requirements.txt requirements-dev.txt Jenkinsfile README.md .github/workflows/main.yml fitness_gui_demo.py filesummary.md execution_validation_report.html execution_evidence
git diff --cached --check
git diff --cached --stat
git commit -m "Add complete ACEest Fitness application and DevOps workflow"
git push origin main

Jenkins VM configuration and run

To execute the pipeline in Jenkins:

  1. Sign in to Jenkins in the Linux VM and open the ACEest Fitness Gym-CI job.
  2. For job configuration, use Pipeline script from SCM, SCM Git, repository https://github.com/malli19960/aceest-fitness-devops.git, branch */main, script path Jenkinsfile. Save the job.
  3. Choose Build Now to run it manually; open the new build number and Console Output to see checkout and stage results.
  4. For push-triggered builds, enable GitHub hook trigger for GITScm polling and configure the GitHub webhook to call https://<jenkins-host>/github-webhook/.

The Jenkinsfile runs Build and Lint (currently only the Docker test-image build), Test, and Build Runtime Image in that order; it does not deploy or start a long-running app container. The job description is “Builds and tests the ACEest Fitness application using Docker, then builds the runtime image.”

VM buildObserved result
#1Failed immediately: no Pipeline flow definition was configured.
#2Historical failure: Jenkins loaded the Jenkinsfile and checked out main, but Docker socket access was denied; Test and runtime-image stages were skipped.
#9SUCCESS - At revision 13b2562, Jenkins built the test image, passed all 33 container tests, and built the runtime image. Open Build #9 Console Output in the VM.

Successful Jenkins Build #9 evidence

After Docker group membership was applied to the Jenkins service and Jenkins restarted, the job ran successfully. These screenshots show the result, the 33-test container stage, and the final pipeline status.

Resolution and verification: an administrator added jenkins to the docker group and restarted the Jenkins service to refresh its supplementary groups. The approved administrator commands were:

sudo usermod -aG docker jenkins
sudo systemctl restart jenkins
id jenkins
sudo -u jenkins docker info --format '{{.ServerVersion}}'

id jenkins then showed the docker group, and Docker Engine verification returned version 27.5.1. Jenkins Build #9 then completed all pipeline stages with SUCCESS; its container test stage passed all 33 tests and the runtime image built successfully. The earlier Build #2 screenshot above records the permission issue before this fix.

Operational issue and resolution

IssueCauseResolution and verification
Docker build denied in JenkinsThe Docker socket is root:docker with group-only access; the Jenkins service initially lacked the docker supplementary group.An administrator ran usermod -aG docker jenkins and restarted Jenkins. The Jenkins identity then reported the group, Docker Engine access worked as the Jenkins user, and Build #9 passed all stages.
Docker service availabilityThe Linux VM daemon must be running before building or starting containers.Run sudo systemctl start docker; systemctl is-active docker returned active before manual validation.

Scope and limitations

Docker/VM status: Docker CLI is not installed on the local Windows machine, but the Linux assignment VM successfully built both images, ran the container tests (33 passed), and smoke-tested the runtime API after sudo systemctl start docker. Jenkins Build #2 still failed at the Docker socket: its service account is not in the docker group. GitHub Actions runs #4 and #5 passed.

The desktop startup check confirms window construction and event processing, not every interactive workflow. The main Flask application behavior is covered by the automated test suite. Historical reference files are excluded from this report and were not run.
